1.why: Token verification requires record.sessionId === session.id (plus a constant accountBinding), so the code is tied to the requesting session, though there is no real user account model to bind to.

2.why: A reset token is rejected unless record.sessionId matches the current session's id, so it cannot be replayed from another browser/session.

3.why: Nothing in /api/password invalidates or rotates session ids or clears the sessions map — the same session cookie (and any other existing session) remains valid after the password change.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key, HSTS, upgrade-insecure-requests, and rejects non-https URLs, but no minimum TLS version is explicitly pinned (relies on Bun defaults).

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 digests and passwords via Bun.password.hash bcrypt cost 10, which are appropriate algorithms for these secrets.

6.why: There is no email delivery at all; instead the raw recovery token and MFA code are returned in the JSON response and printed verbatim in the on-page Logs panel and console, so nothing is hidden or guarded.

7.why: Inputs are type-checked and constrained (contact length/control-char filter, token regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$, 6-digit MFA regex, 2 KB body cap) and output uses textContent only.

8.why: The app issues no redirects or outbound fetches whatsoever and CSP sets form-action 'self', base-uri 'none', so no unsafe redirect target exists.

9.why: No email templates exist, and the only HTML template injects just a nonce and a JSON-escaped CSRF token — no user-supplied data is placed in markup.

10.why: Error responses are generic and stack-trace free, but the recovery token and MFA confirmation code are deliberately written to console.log and the visible Logs panel.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, yet the MFA confirmation code is hardcoded in source as "482916" and the accountBinding string is also a literal in the code.

12.why: There are no default user accounts or credentials, but the fixed hardcoded MFA code 482916 functions as a known default secret for every session.

13.why: Rate limiting exists (3 recovery/15 min, 6 verifications/10 min, 5 token attempts then burn, 5 MFA attempts then 60 s lock), though counters are session-scoped and reset by discarding the cookie.

14.why: The recovery endpoint always returns the same neutral message: "If the contact can be used for recovery, instructions have been prepared."

15.why: Tokens are 32 bytes from crypto.getRandomValues, base64url-encoded, single-use, 10-minute lifetime, and bound to the issuing session.
